Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 31, verses 16–19:

Explanation of the words:

*Innaha in taku mithqala habbatin*: i.e., there exists the weight of a grain of mustard seed.

*Fa-takun fi sakhratin*: i.e., inside one of the rocks, where no one knows it.

*Latif khabir*: i.e., Subtle (latif) in extracting the grain, Aware (khabir) of its place wherever it is.

*Wa'mur bi'l-ma'ruf wa'nha 'ani'l-munkar*: i.e., command the people to obey God the Exalted, and forbid them from disobeying Him.

*Min 'azm al-umur*: i.e., of the matters God has commanded as firm obligations, with no concession (rukhsa) permitted in them.

*Wa la tusa''ir khaddaka lil-nas*: i.e., do not turn your face away from the one you are speaking to out of arrogance.

*Marahan*: i.e., strutting, walking with conceit.

*Mukhtal fakhur*: i.e., swaggering and boastful, much given to pride in what God has bestowed, and not giving thanks.

*Wa'qsid fi mashyika*: i.e., proceed with deliberation and do not hasten in your walk, nor act arrogantly.

*Wa'ghdud min sawtika*: i.e., lower your voice, which is moderation in speech.

*Inna ankar al-aswat*: i.e., the most hideous and most detestable of voices among people, because its beginning is an exhalation (zafir) and its end an inhalation (shahiq).

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the story of Luqman, peace be upon him. God, the Exalted, says, reporting Luqman's words to his son Tharan: ﴿O my son, indeed it, if it should be the weight of a grain of mustard seed﴾, i.e., if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed of good or evil, of a good deed or a bad deed, ﴿and it be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, God will bring it forth﴾, and will call to account for it and recompense for it, ﴿indeed God is Subtle﴾, i.e., in extracting it, ﴿Aware﴾ of its place. Accordingly, do righteous deeds, avoid evil deeds, and trust in the recompense of God, the Just and the Merciful. This is what the first verse [16] indicates. As for the second verse [17], it contains the command of his son to establish the prayer, enjoin the good, forbid the evil, and be patient over the harm that comes from that. So he said to him what God, the Exalted, reported of him in His words: ﴿O my son, establish the prayer﴾, i.e., perform it with its conditions, pillars, obligations and recommended practices; ﴿and enjoin the good﴾, i.e., obedience to God in what He has made obligatory upon His servants; ﴿and forbid the evil﴾, i.e., from what God the Exalted has forbidden His servants, whether in belief, speech or action. ﴿And be patient over what befalls you﴾ of harm from those you command and forbid. His words ﴿indeed that is of the firm matters﴾ mean: indeed establishing the prayer, enjoining good, forbidding evil, and being patient over harm for the sake of God are among the obligatory matters that are firm duties, not concessions.

His words, may He be exalted, ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾: this is among what Luqman said to his son, forbidding him from blameworthy and forbidden traits, namely arrogance toward people, by addressing them while turning away from them with his face, twisting his neck, and the gait of strutting, conceit and haughtiness, and boasting of blessings while not giving thanks for them. His words, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed God does not love every arrogant boaster﴾: this is among what Luqman said to his son when he forbade him from arrogance, conceit and boasting, informing him that God, the Exalted, does not love one in such a state, until his son, whom he admonishes with it and with other things, avoids it.

His words in verse [19]: ﴿And be moderate in your walking﴾, i.e., walk deliberately, without haste or hurrying, since moderation is the opposite of extravagance.

His words: ﴿And lower your voice﴾: he commanded him to be moderate in his voice as well, so that he does not raise his voice except to the extent of need, just as the moderate person does not spend his dirham except when needed and in the amount needed. His words ﴿Indeed the most hideous of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾: he mentioned this sentence to repel him from raising his voice without need, informing him that the most hideous voice is the voice of donkeys, because it is loud and high-pitched, its beginning an exhalation and its end an inhalation. This is the last of what God, the Exalted, related of the story of Luqman, the righteous servant, peace be upon him.

Guidance from the verses:

1) The obligation of being mindful of God and of not belittling good or evil deeds, however small they are.

2) The obligation to establish the prayer, enjoin the good, forbid the evil, and be patient over the harm that befalls the one who enjoins and forbids.

3) The prohibition of arrogance in walking, and the obligation of moderation in walking and speech, so one does not hasten or raise his voice except to the extent of need.

Explanation of the words:

*Wa man yuslim wajhahu ila Allah* (And whoever submits his face to Allah): i.e., he turns to His obedience, sincerely devoting worship to Him, not turning to anyone else among all His creation.

*Wa huwa muhsin* (While he is a doer of good): i.e., and while he is a doer of good in his obedience, through sincerity and following (the Prophet's example).

*Faqad istamsaka bil-'urwati al-wuthqa* (Then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold): i.e., he has clung to the most secure thing one can cling to, so he does not fear its severance in any way.

*Wa ila Allah 'aqibatu al-umur* (And to Allah is the outcome of all matters): i.e., the return of all matters is to Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

*Numatti'uhum qaliylan* (We let them enjoy for a little): i.e., a brief enjoyment in this world, until the end of their appointed terms.

*Thumma nadtarruhum ila 'adhabin ghalidh* (Then We will compel them to a harsh punishment): i.e., then in the Hereafter We will force them into the punishment of the Fire. *Al-ghalid* means heavy.

*Qul al-hamdu lillah* (Say: "All praise is due to Allah"): i.e., praise Allah for the manifestation of the proof, by saying "All praise is due to Allah."

*La ya'lamun* (They do not know): i.e., who deserves praise and thanks and who does not, due to their ignorance.

The meaning of the verses:

After establishing the proof against the polytheists for worshipping other than Allah and for following their fathers in polytheism, evil, and corruption, Allah, the Exalted, said, encouraging salvation and calling to reform: ﴿And whoever submits his face to Allah﴾, i.e., turns his face and heart toward his Lord, worshipping Him, humbled before Him, submissive to His command and prohibition. ﴿While he is a doer of good﴾, i.e., while he is a doer of good in his worship, sincere in it for Allah, and following the Messenger of Allah in its performance. ﴿Then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾, i.e., he has taken hold of the most secure end, so he never fears its severance. The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And to Allah is the outcome of all matters﴾ inform that the return of all matters is to Allah, who decides concerning them as He wills. So let the servant entrust all his affairs to Allah, since they all return to Him, thereby gaining a favor with his Lord. His words to His Messenger: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you﴾, i.e., submit your face to your Lord, entrust your affair to Him, relying upon Him, and whoever among mankind disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you, i.e., do not be concerned with it nor grieve over it. ﴿To Us is their return﴾, i.e., their return is to Us after their death and resurrection. ﴿Then We will inform them of what they did﴾ in this abode of evil and wickedness, and We will recompense them for it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, i.e., of the beliefs and intentions that they conceal and hide. By this the reckoning will be precise and the recompense swift. His words, the Exalted: ﴿We will let them enjoy for a little﴾, i.e., We give respite to these polytheists and do not hasten their punishment, so they enjoy the term of their lives, which is a brief enjoyment. ﴿Then We will compel them﴾ after their death and resurrection ﴿to a harsh punishment﴾, i.e., We will force them by compulsion into a severe, heavy punishment that cannot be endured or borne, which is the punishment of the Fire. We seek refuge with Allah from it and from every deed that leads to it. His words, the Exalted, in verse [25]: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ i.e., if you asked these polytheists, O Our Messenger, saying to them: "Who created the heavens and the earth?", they would hasten to answer, saying "Allah." Then say, "All praise is due to Allah" for establishing the proof against you by your own acknowledgment. And since Allah is the Creator and Provider, how can He be worshipped alongside others or instead of Him? Where are the minds of these people? His words: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, i.e., they do not know the requirement of praise nor its implication, nor who deserves praise and who does not, for they are ignorant people who know nothing.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., by creation, dominion, and servitude. Therefore He is independent of the polytheists and their worship, so do not grieve over them nor concern yourself with them, whether they worship or not. ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Free of need﴾ from all that is other than Him, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., praised for His great actions and beautiful creation.

Guidance from the verses:

1) Clarification of the salvation of the people of "There is no god but Allah," those who worshipped Allah alone in the manner He prescribed through His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ.

2) Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense.

3) Clarification that the Arab polytheists were monotheists in lordship but polytheists in worship, as is the state of many people today, who believe that Allah is the Lord of everything and there is no lord other than Him, yet they slaughter, make vows, and swear by other than Him, and fear and dread others besides Him. We seek refuge with Allah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 31, verses 29–32:

Explanation of the words:

"Alam tara" (Have you not seen): i.e., have you not known, O addressee.

"Anna Allaha yuliju al-layla fi al-nahar" (That God causes the night to enter into the day): i.e., He makes a part of it enter into the day, and makes a part of the day enter into the night, according to the seasons.

"Wa sakhkhara al-shams wa al-qamar" (And He has subjected the sun and the moon): they glide in their orbits for all time, neither of them tiring, until the Day of Resurrection, which is their appointed term.

"Dhalika bi-anna Allaha huwa al-haqq" (That is because God is the Truth): i.e., that which has been mentioned of causing the night to enter the day and subjecting, is because God is the true deity.

"Wa anna ma yad'una min dunihi al-batil" (And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood): i.e., and that what they call upon besides Him of deities is falsehood.

"Bi-ni'mati Allah" (By the favour of God): i.e., by His bounty upon the servants and His kindness to them, in that He prepared the means of their running.

"Li-kulli sabbarin shakur" (For everyone who is steadfast and grateful): i.e., steadfast in refraining from sins, grateful for blessings.

"Wa idha ghashiyahum mawj" (And when a wave covers them): i.e., rises over them and envelops them from above.

"Ka-al-zulal" (Like canopies): i.e., like mountains that shade what is beneath them.

"Fa-minhum muqtasid" (Among them is one of moderation): i.e., between disbelief and belief, meaning one who is balanced in that, neither believing nor disbelieving.

"Kullu khattarin kafur" (Every treacherous ingrate): i.e., a treacherous one, ungrateful for the blessings of God the Exalted.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns establishing monotheism and refuting polytheism and disbelief. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Have you not seen﴾, i.e., have you not known, O Prophet, that God, the One possessing divinity over any other, ﴿causes the night to enter into the day﴾ by making a part of it enter the day, ﴿and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ by making a part of it enter the night, and that is according to the annual seasons; ﴿and He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾, both gliding in their orbits for the benefit of mankind until an appointed term, i.e., until a specific time determined by Him, the Exalted, which is the Day of Resurrection. And God, the Exalted, is aware of what you do: nothing of your deeds, good or bad, is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for them. His saying ﴿That is because God is the Truth﴾ means that this causing of the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night, and the subjecting of the sun and moon, and God's knowledge of the deeds of His servants and His recompense for them, is a decisive proof, removing every doubt, that God is the true God, and that what they call upon besides Him of idols is falsehood. It also decisively establishes that God, the Exalted, who possesses true divinity, is the Most High, the Great, i.e., the One of absolute, great exaltedness, greater than which there is nothing, for He is the Lord and Owner of everything, its Subduer and Controller. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 31, verses 33–34:

Explanation of the Words

"Ittaqu rabbakum" (Fear your Lord): i.e., fear Him, so believe in Him, worship Him alone, and you will be saved from His punishment.

"Wakhshaw yawman" (And fear a Day): i.e., fear the Day of Reckoning and what takes place in it.

"La yajzi walidun 'an waladihi" (No father will avail anything for his child): i.e., no father will suffice in that Day to avail his child in anything.

"Inna wa'da Allahi haqq" (Indeed, the promise of Allah is true): i.e., Allah's promise of reckoning and recompense is a established truth; it will certainly come to be.

"La taghurrannakumu al-hayat al-dunya" (Let not the worldly life deceive you): i.e., do not be deceived by the worldly life, for it is transient; so submit, and you will be safe.

"Wa la yaghurrannakum billahi al-gharur" (And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah): i.e., Satan seizes upon Allah's forbearance toward you and His granting you respite, so he emboldens you toward sins and procrastinates you in repentance.

"Wa yunazzilu al-ghayth" (And He sends down the rain): i.e., the rain.

"Wa ya'lamu ma fi al-arham" (And He knows what is in the wombs): i.e., whether it is male or female, and none other than Him knows that.

"Madha taksibu ghadan" (What one will earn tomorrow): i.e., of good or evil, and Allah knows it.

Meaning of the Two Noble Verses

This is a general call to all mankind, in which their Lord, exalted is He, advises them to be mindful of Him by believing in Him and worshipping Him alone without partner, and to fear a tremendous Day containing terrors and great events whose extent cannot be measured, such that no father will avail his child and no child will avail his father in anything, since each one desires only the salvation of his own self, saying "myself, myself." This is due to the severity of the terror, a Day on which no one will avail another in anything, even the closest relative. It is a Day that will certainly come, for Allah has promised it to people, and Allah's promise is true, and Allah does not break His promise. On that basis He says to them: ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾ with its pleasures, its adornments, and long life within it, ﴿and let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah﴾, the Possessor of forbearance and generosity, ﴿the Deceiver﴾, i.e., Satan, from among men or jinn, who drives you to delay repentance and to engage in various sins by beautifying them for you and encouraging you toward them. So be alert, for death is inevitable and may come suddenly. Repentance, repentance, O servants of Allah! This is the advice of the Lord, blessed and exalted, to His servants, so is there anyone who will respond? This is what the first verse [33] indicates.

As for the second verse [34], Allah, majestic is His majesty, informs His servants that He alone holds the knowledge of the Hour, when it will come, and when the Resurrection will take place, and that no one whoever he may be can know that. This is a condition requiring the servant to hasten repentance and not delay it. Just as He, exalted, alone holds the knowledge of the time of the descent of rain, whether on a day, a night, or an hour of night or day. And He knows what is in the wombs of females, whether male or female, white or red or black, and of tallness or shortness, and of belief or disbelief, and none other than Him knows that. And He knows what each person will earn tomorrow, of good or evil, wealth or poverty, and He knows in what land of the earth each soul will die and its dwelling place, and none knows that except Allah. Therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The keys of the Unseen are five," and he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾ "Related in the Sahih."

As for His saying "Indeed Allah is Knowing", i.e., of everything, and not only these five, Acquainted with everything, minute or great, of essences, attributes and states, and with the inner aspects of matters as with their outer aspects. For this reason He alone must be worshipped, by what He has prescribed of the kinds of worship, which are the ladder of success, the ascent to perfection, and felicity in both abodes.

Guidance of the Two Verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1) The obligation of fearing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by believing in Him and affirming His oneness in worship.

2) Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

3) Warning against being deceived by the worldly life, and warning against Satan, i.e., against following him and being deluded by what he beautifies and makes appealing of sins.

4) Explanation of the five keys of the Unseen and the exclusivity of the Lord, exalted, in knowing them.

5) Everyone who claims knowledge of the Unseen, whether among jinn or men, is a tyrant (taghut) who must be cursed and opposed.

6) What is claimed today, that by means of modern instruments one has known what is in a woman's womb, this knowledge does not fall under His saying ﴿and He knows what is in the wombs﴾, because it is like one who opens the belly and looks at what is in it and then says it is such-and-such, and that is due to the presence of reflecting rays. As for what is excluded from every limit except Allah, it is that a person says: "In the belly of so-and-so's wife is a male or a female," and does not approach her, nor test her in her previous birth, nor attempt in any way to know what is in her belly.

As for His saying "Indeed Allah is Knowing", i.e., of everything, and not only these five, Acquainted with everything, minute or great, of essences, attributes and states, and with the inner aspects of matters as with their outer aspects. For this reason He alone must be worshipped, by what He has prescribed of the kinds of worship, which are the ladder of success, the ascent to perfection, and felicity in both abodes.

Guidance of the Two Verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1) The obligation of fearing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by believing in Him and affirming His oneness in worship.

2) Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

3) Warning against being deceived by the worldly life, and warning against Satan, i.e., against following him and being deluded by what he beautifies and makes appealing of sins.

4) Explanation of the five keys of the Unseen and the exclusivity of the Lord, exalted, in knowing them.

5) Everyone who claims knowledge of the Unseen, whether among jinn or men, is a tyrant (taghut) who must be cursed and opposed.

6) What is claimed today, that by means of modern instruments one has known what is in a woman's womb, this knowledge does not fall under His saying ﴿and He knows what is in the wombs﴾, because it is like one who opens the belly and looks at what is in it and then says it is such-and-such, and that is due to the presence of reflecting rays. As for what is excluded from every limit except Allah, it is that a person says: "In the belly of so-and-so's wife is a male or a female," and does not approach her, nor test her in her previous birth, nor attempt in any way to know what is in her belly.
